arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The employee's advocate argued oral reports deserve protection. He emphasized the practical reality of workplace reporting.
The employer's advocate argued the law requires formal procedures. He stressed the need for clear documentation.
The government advocate noted many statutes share similar provisions. He highlighted the broader legal landscape.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of the Fair Labor Standards Act. It asks if the statute covers informal verbal reports. The lower court ruled against the employee. The employee seeks reversal of that judgment.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The employee wants the court to reverse the lower court judgment. He seeks protection for his oral report.
The employer wants the court to affirm the lower court judgment. It seeks to limit protection to written filings.
